theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners is the headline/leader theme with the highest durability bar (0.73), full breadth (1.0), and an eligible absolute-trend gate. The supporting legs are trend-gate (the validated drawdown-control leg) and durability/cohesion (breadth 1.0 suggests the whole group is participating). Momentum rank is only a focus lens, not an alpha signal, so the lean is a modest trend-following tilt conditioned on the trend gate staying intact.
theses.dissent: Gold Miners' r10 is -0.0664, showing recent short-term weakness; hurst_tag is 'mixed' meaning the trend is not cleanly persistent, and relative momentum has rank-IC ~0, so the leadership may be stale flow rather than durable alpha.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO closes below its 50-day moving average and the durability_bar for ca_gold drops below 0.5 before the 30-day check-by date

theses.subject: Silver & Royalties
theses.thesis: Silver & Royalties is the challenger in the same precious-metals complex, eligible with a high durability bar (0.67) and full breadth (1.0). It shares the same trend-gate discipline with the leader. The rotation margin to the leader is narrow (0.147), and both benefit from the same macro/commodity narrative, so a modest paired tilt within the complex is defensible as trend-following, not rotation-timing.
theses.dissent: hurst_tag is 'mean-revert' for Silver & Royalties, signalling the trend is not persistent and may snap back; momentum rank has no forward edge, so this lean rests entirely on the trend gate and complex cohesion, which can break quickly in precious metals.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO (shared proxy with Gold Miners) lags the S&P/TSX benchmark by 5% or more over any rolling 20-day window before the check-by date

theses.subject: Big Banks
theses.thesis: Big Banks is eligible and has a 'trend' hurst_tag, but its breadth is very weak (0.286) suggesting participation is narrow. The trend-gate is the only validated edge, and while the gate keeps it eligible, the poor breadth and middling durability (0.59) argue against leaning into it when a cleaner trend-following alternative (precious metals) exists. This is a relative-avoid within the eligible set, not a short.
theses.dissent: Big Banks has a clean 'trend' tag and stable non-mean-reverting behaviour, which historically is exactly what the absolute-trend gate rewards; avoiding it may give up a genuinely persistent trend for a 'mixed' precious-metals leader with a negative r10.
